questions.question: In literary analysis, what is a theme?
choices: the subject named in one word
a message or insight about life developed by a text

questions.question: “Friendship” names a broad subject. What would turn it into a theme statement?
choices: Trust grows when people support one another through difficulty.

questions.question: A theme should be supported by what?
choices: patterns and events in the text

questions.question: A character refuses help, fails, then succeeds after accepting advice. Which theme is best supported?
choices: cooperation can help people meet difficult goals

questions.question: A story shows a student returning a lost wallet even though no one saw the choice. Which idea is best supported?
choices: integrity is shown through choices made without an audience

questions.question: Two characters disagree but listen and revise their views. What theme could this develop?
choices: silence is the only path to peace

questions.question: A traveler reaches a goal but realizes the journey changed what matters to them. What theme might fit?
choices: experiences can reshape a person’s priorities

questions.question: A story’s topic is “ambition.” Which is a theme rather than a topic?
choices: Ambition without regard for others can cause harm.
The story takes place at school.

questions.question: A student reads a short story about one contest winner and writes, “Everyone should always follow every dream.” What is the main weakness?
choices: It generalizes beyond what the story establishes.
It names only a broad subject, not an insight.
It summarizes a single plot event.
It describes setting instead of meaning.

questions.question: A character gains recognition but loses close friendships through dishonesty. Which theme is most supported?
choices: achievement may carry a cost when pursued without integrity
recognition is the same as happiness

questions.question: A story ends with a community restoring a damaged park together. Which theme best fits the repeated actions?
choices: shared responsibility can improve a community

questions.question: A character learns that asking questions is a strength, not a weakness. Which theme statement expresses the insight?
choices: Curiosity can support learning and confidence.

questions.question: To identify a theme, readers should connect what elements?
choices: page numbers, chapter titles, and font
author biography and publication date only
setting names and dialogue tags only
character choices, consequences, and recurring ideas

questions.question: A story repeats images of locked doors, while its character slowly learns to speak honestly. Which theme is best supported?
choices: honesty can open paths to connection

questions.question: A narrator says “be brave,” but the plot rewards a character who carefully asks for help. What should a theme claim rely on most?
choices: the text’s full pattern of choices and consequences

questions.question: A character gives up a prize to keep a promise. What theme does that decision most directly support?
choices: competition is harmful in every case

questions.question: A story presents success after several failures, with reflection after each attempt. Which theme is best supported?
choices: failure is always caused by others
learning from setbacks can lead to progress

questions.question: A text includes both a generous mentor and a selfish leader. How can their contrasting outcomes develop theme?
choices: contrasting them reveals the exact setting
comparing their choices shows how values affect relationships
differences remove the need for evidence

questions.question: A student claims the theme is “technology.” What revision makes it an arguable insight?
choices: Technology can connect people while also changing how they communicate.

questions.question: A story’s ending leaves a conflict partly unresolved but shows the character accepting responsibility. Which theme is most defensible?
choices: every conflict must have a perfect ending
taking responsibility can matter even when problems remain
